identity.name: Tank Louis Cartier

case.bezel: flat sapphire crystal, rectangular case, no bezel

identity.one_liner: The rounded-corner, curved-side reading of Louis Cartier's 1919 Tank, sold under its own name since the early 1920s and still the brand's reference mechanical dress watch.

provenance_events.description: Louis Cartier designs the Tank Louis in 1917 (filed 1917, sold 1919), inspired by the Renault FT-17 tank seen in WWI. The Tank becomes Cartier's most-photographed watch — worn by Andy Warhol, Jackie Kennedy, Yves Saint Laurent, and a dozen U.S. presidents.

narrative.story: Louis Cartier designed the original Tank in 1919, its parallel case sides drawn from the aerial silhouette of the Renault FT tanks then arriving on the Western Front. The Tank Louis Cartier followed in the early 1920s as a softer reading of that shape, curving the brancards and swapping the apple-form hands for sword hands, and it has stayed close to that silhouette in continuous production ever since.
narrative.collector_notes: The Tank Louis Cartier is sold across many sizes and materials, from a mini quartz in yellow gold to large automatic pieces on caliber 1899 MC; the reference here (WGTA0211) is the medium manual-wind version on caliber 1917 MC, and specs should always be checked against the specific size rather than the family name alone. Jacqueline Kennedy wore a Cartier Tank through much of her White House years, and Andy Warhol was photographed in various Tank Louis Cartier watches through the 1970s and 80s.
